sub_scenario.family: communicating uncertainty and risk escalation in cross-functional decisions
sub_scenario.one_line: hospital partnership coordinator: request the missing process details

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the referral log and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The partner diary review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can arrange a standard referral in the afternoon when every service has confirmed capacity.
Are afternoon referrals inherently unsafe?
No, complete information makes them straightforward.
Someone new shadowed me in the care coordination desk this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the winter surge into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
In a complex discharge escalation, I named home nursing as the cause of a delay before separating the ward notes from an unreturned family call, and the team pursued the wrong gap.
How was it resolved?
We waited for the missing call and found a transport issue instead.
I can lead a morning coordination call when the discharge notes distinguish confirmed needs from pending tests.
What does that achieve?
It stops the group from sending a patient to the wrong service.
I archived last cycle's notes on the partner diary and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
At 15:30 I am less able to reconcile conflicting notes after a full day of referrals.
Does that mean you cannot join?
It means the format needs clear limits on what is decided live.
A vendor call about the referral log ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the care coordination desk checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the winter surge.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the partner diary records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The partnership office asks whether you can attend daily 15:30 escalation office hours, but the invitation does not say whether referrals may be assigned there or only reviewed.
What information is missing?
I need to know the authority, records, and follow-up process before giving a yes or no.
I sketched next week's plan for the winter surge before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the referral log updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
A next-morning multidisciplinary huddle is available for cases that cannot be verified during the office hour.
Does that settle the invitation?
It helps, but I still need the office-hour rules.
The chief operating officer says a prompt RSVP would reassure partner organizations.
Does that supply the missing detail?
No, reassurance does not define a safe escalation process.
I closed the week by updating the care coordination desk handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The partnership office asks me to RSVP to its daily 15:30 escalation hour, but its decision authority and record requirements are unspecified. What should I reply?
